headline: NSA guidance names tool poisoning and weak credentials as core MCP security risks
lede: According to aigovernance.com, the NSA issued a cybersecurity information sheet on MCP that names tool poisoning, weak authentication, inadequate human approval and absent audit logs as core failure modes. Cloudflare separately says it has formed a coalition to standardize signed, delegated agent identity.

items.title: NSA information sheet lists core MCP failure modes and countermeasures
items.body: aigovernance.com, citing Cranium AI, reports that the U.S. National Security Agency issued a cybersecurity information sheet on MCP security risks. The sheet reportedly identifies four failure modes: tool poisoning, weak or missing authentication, inadequate human approval workflows, and absent audit logs. Its countermeasures include pinning and reviewing tool definitions before use, short-lived credentials scoped to minimum access, isolating MCP servers, validating tool inputs and outputs, and logging agent and user identity on every invocation.
items.why_it_matters: MCP server and client operators can check their deployments against this list: pinned tool definitions, scoped short-lived credentials, server isolation and per-call identity logging. aigovernance.com argues regulated teams will be measured against it.

items.title: Cloudflare announces Trusted Agent Delegation coalition built on Web Bot Auth
items.body: According to Reveneau, Cloudflare announced the Trusted Agent Delegation coalition on 5 November 2026. The coalition's goal is one open standard for how an agent proves who sent it, covering identity, reputation and accountability. Cloudflare describes the partners only by category and names no individual company. Cloudflare says it builds on Web Bot Auth for per-request signatures and on MOLE, a protocol for per-person rate limiting with an anonymous identifier. The coalition also plans a machine-readable Site Agent Access Policy file.
items.why_it_matters: Agent builders choosing between custom headers and signed requests should look at Web Bot Auth. Site operators should watch for the Site Agent Access Policy format, which would declare which agents a site accepts and at which identity level.

items.title: Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI back a new AI training opt-out proposal
items.body: A Knight-Georgetown Institute commentary by Alissa Cooper says Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI all announced plans to support a new mechanism that lets publishers opt out of having their content used for AI training. The proposal was authored by Anthropic's Kevin Kelley. Cooper argues that the coverage left out how the proposal relates to the IETF AIPREF effort, which builds in part on RFC 9309, the Robots Exclusion Protocol.
items.why_it_matters: Publishers who already express preferences in robots.txt or through AIPREF drafts should track how the new mechanism relates to the IETF vocabulary before adopting it.

items.title: AG-UI Kotlin SDK 0.5.0 aligns with AG-UI 1.0, with breaking validation changes
items.body: The AG-UI release of 2026-11-05 published kotlin-core, kotlin-client and kotlin-tools 0.5.0 to Maven Central. The release targets AG-UI 1.0 and adds REASONING_* events, deprecating THINKING_* events. It also adds interrupt protocol support on RUN_FINISHED outcomes and ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT/ACTIVITY_DELTA events. The notes warn that strict event and input decoding may reject previously accepted payloads. The release of 2026-11-06 published ag-ui-openai-agents 0.1.0 on PyPI, without approved release notes.
items.why_it_matters: Kotlin integrators upgrading to 0.5.0 should test payloads that older versions accepted, and migrate THINKING_* handling to REASONING_* events.

items.title: Cashfree adds WebMCP tools to its Hosted Checkout
items.body: Cashfree says its Hosted Checkout now publishes WebMCP tools that browser agents can call. Agents can use them to read the order, find a payment method and show a UPI QR code for the user to pay. Cashfree says merchants do not need to change their integrations. Support covers redirect mode, and UPI QR payments work on the desktop layout. Cashfree says agents need a Chromium-based browser.
items.why_it_matters: This is a payment-provider deployment of WebMCP, which is still a Draft Community Group Report. Agent developers can test checkout flows against it rather than parsing the page.

sources.title: Cashfree launches Checkout for Agents on WebMCP

items.title: Scraping Agency index: training crawlers are blocked far more often than AI search bots
items.body: Scraping Agency reports that 29.6% of sites with a robots.txt fully block at least one AI training crawler (151 of 510 sites). According to its index, 21.2% block OpenAI's GPTBot, versus 11.2% for OAI-SearchBot. It also reports that 3.3% publish Cloudflare-style Content Signals in robots.txt (17 of 510 sites).
items.why_it_matters: Operators of crawlers and fetchers should expect training and search user agents to be treated differently. Using separate, documented tokens per purpose affects how much of the web each crawler can reach.

items.title: Panel: three docs sites drop MCP and Server Cards, while descope.com adds them
items.body: Our panel counted MCP on 135 of 278 domains (-2 since 2026-11-06) and MCP Server Cards on 122 of 278 (-2 since 2026-11-06). docs.gladia.io, docs.incident.io and docs.kombo.dev stopped publishing both. docs.incident.io moved from grade A+ (60) to B (38), and docs.kombo.dev from A+ (60) to B (43). descope.com began publishing both and moved from grade B (30) to A+ (67). The official MCP Registry saw 1911 servers (3000 versions) published or updated since 2026-11-06.
items.why_it_matters: Simultaneous drops across several docs sites can indicate a shared hosting or platform change. Publishers relying on such platforms should verify their MCP endpoints still resolve.
